skill.name: appllama-usage
skill.description: Use the Appllama MCP (mcp.appllama.io) well — research real top-grossing mobile apps, their screens, flows, and UI elements, then build from what you learn. Load when the Appllama MCP is connected and the task involves building a mobile app or screen, researching app design patterns, studying onboarding/paywall/feature flows, improving an existing screen, or whenever an appllama_* / search_apps / list_app_screens tool is available. Covers the tool map, pagination, expiring media, and the full build-from-research playbooks.

content.value_statement: Mobile teams often design from isolated inspiration and miss the patterns that shape successful app journeys. This skill guides structured research of top-grossing apps, screens, flows, and UI elements before implementation.
actual_capabilities: Explains the Appllama MCP tool map for apps, screens, flows, UI elements, and boards.
Guides sequential pagination and durable screen reference workflows.
Structures cross-app research around onboarding, paywalls, navigation, and product journeys.
Provides a build-from-scratch playbook from research through simulator verification.
Provides a screen-improvement playbook with keyword and semantic reference searches.
Recommends local notes and media organization for research findings.
limitations: It does not build, edit, or test an application by itself.
It requires access to the Appllama MCP and available account credits.
Media URLs expire, so references must be reviewed or refreshed promptly.
Research guidance does not replace platform design review, legal review, or usability testing.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Mobile Product
use_cases.description: Study comparable apps, map their journeys, and turn observed patterns into a focused screen and navigation specification.

use_cases.title: Improve an Existing Screen
use_cases.description: Diagnose hierarchy, motion, and control issues, then compare the screen with targeted references from successful apps.

use_cases.title: Research a Conversion Flow
use_cases.description: Compare onboarding, paywall, welcome, or category-specific flows across apps and identify common patterns worth testing.

prompt_templates.title: Find Basic References
prompt_templates.prompt: Research top-grossing apps for my mobile app category. Identify five relevant apps and summarize their main flows and screen counts.

prompt_templates.title: Study an Onboarding Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the onboarding flows of three strong apps in my category. For each step, record the user goal, information requested, and value provided.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Reference Board
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a research plan for my target screen using keyword and semantic searches. Select the strongest references and explain the layout, controls, hierarchy, and motion patterns to extract.

prompt_templates.title: Specify and Verify a Product
prompt_templates.prompt: Research the leading apps for my product concept, synthesize a screen-by-screen specification, define navigation and one-way doors, and produce a simulator verification checklist for happy, skeptical, and failure paths.

output_examples.input: Research habit tracker apps with strong onboarding and subscription flows.
output: Shortlist five apps using revenue, rating, downloads, and product fit.
Compare onboarding length, personalization questions, paywall placement, and primary navigation.
Recommend a focused reference set and a research-backed flow outline.

output_examples.input: Improve a workout summary screen that feels visually flat.
output_examples.output: Diagnose the hierarchy, search for keyword and semantic references, then define a stronger layout, control treatment, palette roles, and motion plan.

output_examples.input: Design a new mobile app from research.
output: A journey-ordered screen list with presentation types and back behavior.
A pattern synthesis separating table stakes, useful differentiators, and opportunities.
A simulator checklist covering normal, skipped, offline, interrupted, and invalid-input paths.

best_practices: Start with a named research question and use several apps before forming a pattern.
Study complete journeys in order, including images, states, transitions, and back behavior.
Refresh expired media links and separate durable notes from temporary URLs.
anti_patterns: Do not treat one successful app as proof that a pattern fits every category.
Do not sweep the catalog to extract its dataset instead of answering a real product question.
Do not stop at visual references without specifying states, navigation, and verification paths.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps AI agents research successful mobile apps through the Appllama MCP before designing or improving an app.

faq.question: Does it build the mobile app?
faq.answer: No. It provides research methods, design playbooks, and verification guidance for an agent that performs the implementation.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when the Appllama MCP is available.

faq.question: How does it handle expired media?
faq.answer: It recommends reviewing media promptly and requesting fresh links by durable screen ID when a URL expires.

faq.question: Can it research paywalls and onboarding?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides focused methods for comparing onboarding, paywall, welcome, and category-specific flows.

faq.question: What should teams avoid?
faq.answer: Teams should avoid catalog harvesting, copying watermarked references, and declaring a screen complete without simulator verification.
